bull.t: Clean balance sheet and liquidity runway
bull.b: Streamex's post-quarter capital structure materially reduces near-term solvency risk: zero reported debt, sizable cash/marketable holdings and stated >12 months runway give management time to scale distribution and product-market fit without immediate refinancing, lowering structural liquidity pressure.

bull.t: Live product with operational proof points
bull.b: Having GLDY live with NAV tracking, initial dividend distributions and an attestation underway establishes core operational capability. This demonstrates the firm can mint, custody, compute NAV and execute payouts—foundational systems that materially de-risk commercialization over the coming quarters.

bull.t: Institutional partnerships boosting distribution and liquidity
bull.b: Partnerships with a permissioned AMM, a 24/7 market-maker and a large IRA custodian address two structural hurdles: secondary liquidity and access to retirement accounts. These integrations create durable distribution channels and fee opportunities that support scalable AUM growth and sticky investor access over time.

bear.t: No GAAP revenue and persistent net losses
bear.b: Streamex remains pre-revenue on GAAP terms while reporting large quarterly losses, indicating the business model has not yet converted operational activity into sustainable sales. Persisting negative profitability heightens execution risk: scaling costs may outpace nascent AUM-driven revenues until meaningful scale is reached.

bear.t: Consistent negative operating and free cash flow
bear.b: The company has produced negative operating and free cash flow across reported periods, implying ongoing cash burn. Even with current cash buffers, continued outflows require careful capital management or future raises; prolonged cash deficits could force dilution or constrain investments needed to scale AUM and revenues.

bear.t: High equity-based compensation and governance dilution risk
bear.b: Substantial equity-linked compensation and milestone-driven awards, together with sizable noncash stock-based expense, imply meaningful future dilution risk and concentrated executive influence on the board. This can weaken shareholder alignment and increase capital loading as the company scales, a durable governance and dilution concern.
